patients.label: One-day-old male neonate with multiple congenital anomalies and partial monosomy of chromosome 21q

identity_evidence.quote: We report an interesting case of a neonate from India

attribution_limitations: The neonate is described as one day old at admission, yet the death is stated to occur on the same day, seven hours after birth.
Two different causes of death are stated: multiple congenital anomalies, and severe perinatal asphyxia (HIE grade 3).

The karyotype prints [59%,41%] for the r(21) and del(21) lines, while the metaphase counts are 10 ring chromosome 21 metaphases and 15 long-arm deletion metaphases, so the larger count belongs to the deletion line; the formula also prints 46, X for the ring line although both karyotype panels show an X and a Y.
WGS identified the 21q deletion but the ring chromosome and its breakpoint were not detected.

claims.text: A one-day-old male neonate born at 37 weeks by normal vaginal delivery to a mother with a previous spontaneous abortion weighed 1.340 kg, did not cry, had APGAR scores of 2 and 3 and severe perinatal asphyxia, received bag and mask ventilation, intubation and ventilator support, and died seven hours after birth. Examination showed multiple craniofacial and limb anomalies; echocardiography showed a ventricular septal defect and neurosonogram and fetal autopsy showed holoprosencephaly.
